section_summary.extract_value: This section describes use of the four-factor Intuitive Eating Scale for Adolescents (Dockendorff et al., 2012), with items rated 1 (completely disagree) to 5 (completely agree). Cronbach's α for the four subscales ranged from 0.70 to 0.81 and the overall α was 0.75; CFA retained 16 of 17 items (item 17 did not load) and reported acceptable fit: RMSEA = 0.057, χ2 (110) = 5.13, CFI = 0.935, TLI = 0.919, SRMR = 0.054.
section_summary.evidence_source: The four-factor intuitive eating scale for adolescents (Dockendorff, Petrie, Greenleaf, & Martin, 2012) was used to measure intuitive eating. Participants indicated their agreement with statements (e.g., "I can tell when I'm slightly full") on a 5-point scale ranging from 1 (completely disagree) to 5 (completely agree). Cronbach′ α was 0.70 for Unconditional permission to eat, 0.81 for Eating for physical rather than emotional reasons, 0.81 for Trust in internal hunger/satiety cues, and 0.73 for Awareness of internal hunger/satiety cues. The overall Cronbach's α for intuitive eating was 0.75. CFA was performed to assess the four-factor model. Item 17 was not loaded on any of the four factors, and therefore only 16 items were used in the analysis. The model adequately fit the data, RMSEA = 0.057, χ2 (110) = 5.13, CFI = 0.935, TLI = 0.919, SRMR = 0.054.
